title: Full-Query Security and Mixing of Swap-or-Not
summary: Security is proved only short of the full N-query regime; whether swap-or-not mixes quickly and remains secure for all N queries with a reasonable round count is unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For the swap-or-not shuffle, security has been proven only when the number of queries is less than $(1-\epsilon)N$, while it is conjectured that the construction works well for all $N$ queries with a reasonable number $r$ of rounds, meaning that its mixing time is fast. The unresolved task is to determine whether swap-or-not in fact has fast mixing and adequate security when $q=N$ queries are allowed and $r$ is reasonable.

scope.domain: Symmetric-key security and mixing-time analysis of the swap-or-not shuffle.
parameters: N: full query count corresponding to all available points
epsilon: gap parameter in the proven query threshold
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether swap-or-not has fast mixing and adequate security for q equal to N queries with a reasonable number of rounds.

citations.label: An Enciphering Scheme Based on a Card Shuffle

progress.summary: The paper contrasts its security proof for fewer than (1−epsilon)N queries with an explicit conjecture that swap-or-not works well for N queries and reasonable r. It states that no such full-query result is proved.
